LIFE LONG LEARNERS: individuals who just want to build a better vocabulary.  
MIDDLE SCHOOL: Middle school students who want to lay the foundation for high school or prepare for the SSAT or ISEE.
HIGH SCHOOL: High school students who want to improve the depth of their vocabularies or prepare for the SAT or ACT.

We named the app "The Daily Word", because each morning you will receive a notification with the Word of the Day. When you receive the notification, take a look at the word and see if it is a word that you know. 心に響いた文にはマーカーを引き、また戻ってきたい段落にはブックマークを残せます。どこまで読んだかをアプリが覚えているので、次に開けばその続きから読めます。難しい章は、重要ポイントと要約に先に目を通してから本文に入ると、ぐっと読みやすくなります。フォントと文字の大きさはお好みで選べ、ダークモードにも切り替えられます。

■ アプリを開けば、今日のレッスンが開いています
ワークブックは、一日にひとつのレッスンを一年かけて行う練習です。カレンダーモードをオンにしておけば、1月1日から数えても、自分の進み具合から数えても、今日取り組むレッスンが自動で開きます。

ホーム画面のウィジェットが、今日のワークブックのレッスンのタイトルを表示します。ロックを解除するたびに目に入るので、一日のうちに何度でも今日の考えに立ち返れます。サイズは小と中から選べます。

三冊すべてを朗読で聴けます（AI音声、字幕つき）。画面を消しても再生は続きます。寝る前に流しておけば、スリープタイマーが決めた時間に止めてくれます。朝は設定した時刻に、今日のワークブックのレッスンがアラームのように流れます。

瞑想タイマーをセットして、環境音とともに瞑想します。今日どれだけ瞑想したか、これまでにどれだけ続けてきたかが統計に残ります。

読む、聴く、瞑想する。一日にどれかひとつでもすれば、その日の記録が残り、連続日数がつながっていきます。月間カレンダーではどの日に何をしたかがひと目でわかり、記録が伸びるにつれて励ましの言葉も変わっていきます。

コロンビア大学の臨床心理学者ヘレン・シャックマンが、同僚ウィリアム・セットフォードの助けを得て、1965年から1972年にかけて内なる声を書き取った書物で、1975年に初めて出版されました。赦しを通して世界の見方を変え、分離ではなく一体性の体験へと導きます。テキストは思考体系を説き、ワークブックは一日ひとつのレッスンで一年かけて心を訓練し、教師のためのマニュアルは学ぶ人たちが最もよく抱く問いに答えます。

Claire Kaplan teaches thirteen sudoku techniques, in the order that makes each next one make sense, beginning with the first empty square. Every lesson is played on a real board, and she explains the move in plain language while you make it yourself.

This is a complete sudoku app, and the school sits inside it. Claire teaches one technique at a time.

WHERE DO I START?

Take the placement test. It is five questions, one board each, with no timer and nothing to pass or fail. Claire asks you for the one square that is certain, or the one note that is impossible, and you tap it. You can also tell her you are not sure yet. She credits you with everything easier than the first question you miss, and starts teaching there. You can retake it whenever you like, on fresh boards.

THE THIRTEEN TECHNIQUES, IN ORDER

The White belt teaches the full house, the naked single, and the hidden single, which fill in what is already certain.
The Yellow belt teaches the pointing pair and box line reduction, so you can keep notes and lock digits down.
The Orange belt teaches the naked pair and the hidden pair, which are two squares that share a secret.
The Green belt teaches the naked triple and the hidden triple, which are three of a kind.
The Blue belt teaches the X-Wing, and it is your first fish.
The Purple belt teaches the Y-Wing, the XYZ-Wing, and the Swordfish, which are the wings and the bigger fish.

There are six belts and thirteen lessons in all.

The lessons run on 117 teaching boards, and each one was checked three ways before it shipped. Every board can be finished by the thirteen techniques with no guessing, its hardest required move is exactly the technique the lesson is teaching, and it has exactly one solution. Repeat a lesson and you get a different board.

ONE MINUTE A DAY

The Daily Drill is five questions, drawn from the techniques Claire has taught you. Anything you have stumbled on comes back about twice as often. You cannot fail it. Nothing runs out, and a wrong answer costs you nothing. A wrong tap shakes the board, says "Not that one," and leaves the question open, and you can skip one if you like. Answering quickly earns more points, and answering slowly still earns them, so your best score is a target you set yourself. There is no leaderboard.

BELTS AND CERTIFICATES

Finish every lesson in a belt and Claire awards it. The certificate is a card with the belt, the techniques it covers, the date, and Claire's name. You can share it as a line of plain text.

WHO TEACHES IT

Claire Kaplan teaches every lesson in the app. She stays on the board with you until you find the move yourself.

THE SUDOKU ITSELF

Puzzles are generated on your phone, so you cannot run out. You can play at five difficulties, from Easy through Medium, Hard, and Expert up to Master. The thirteen finish every Easy, Medium and nearly every Hard board. Most Expert boards fall to them, and Master often asks for more. There is one daily puzzle, the same for everyone, on the newspaper ramp from an easy Monday to a Master Saturday. You get pencil notes, unlimited undo, and one hint per puzzle, which fills in a single correct digit. A timer and a mistake tally are both there, and both stay off until you switch them on. You can set the board to light or dark, or to Night, which is a warm red screen for playing in bed.

The streak on your home screen counts any day you did something, whether that was a puzzle, a lesson, or a drill. It cannot be spent or frozen, and nothing scolds you for missing a day.

NO ADS

There are no ads anywhere in the app. Every lesson, every belt, every difficulty, and every daily puzzle is open to you. There is no account and no sign-in, and your progress is stored on your phone. The lessons, the drill, and the daily puzzle all work with no connection. One daily reminder is available in Settings, and it stays off until you turn it on.

Sudoku is a set of moves, and Claire will teach you all thirteen.

results.description:
A little smarter every scroll.

Loup turns the scroll you already do into short lessons from real books — psychology, philosophy, money, productivity, mental health, health and communication — in a feed that never runs out.

HOW IT WORKS

Pick a topic or two, or tell Loup to show you everything.
Swipe up for the next card: a spark (20 seconds), a lesson (about a minute), or a passage of verbatim public-domain text.
Every card is credited to the book and chapter it came from, in Loup's own words.
Like a card and the feed follows that book in chapter order, so you can get through its lessons in about 40 minutes of scrolling.
Skip twice and you're back in your regular feed.
Now and then a wild card turns up, face down, from a shelf you didn't pick. Tap to turn it over.

TOPICS AND BOOKS

Seven topics, drawn from 70 real non-fiction books, for example:
- Psychology: Atomic Habits, Thinking Fast and Slow, Man's Search for Meaning
- Philosophy & Stoicism: Meditations, Seneca's Letters, The Daily Stoic
- Money: The Psychology of Money, Rich Dad Poor Dad, The Intelligent Investor
- Productivity: Deep Work, Digital Minimalism, Essentialism
- Mental health: Dopamine Nation, Stolen Focus, The Body Keeps the Score
- Health & Longevity: Lifespan, Spark
- Communication & Conflict: Nonviolent Communication, Difficult Conversations

New cards are added every week. Loup names these books as the source of its lessons — it is not affiliated with or endorsed by their authors or publishers.

QUICK GAMES IN YOUR FEED

Two short games turn up between the cards from time to time. Quick sort: ten short lines from two of your topics, swipe each one toward the topic it came from. Shootout: a hook from a lesson you've read, and three headings to pick from. A wrong guess costs nothing, and the lesson opens either way. Quick sort can be turned off in your feed options.

YOUR SHELF

Your Profile opens on a shelf holding every book you've read from. The gold on each spine rises as you read, and when you finish a book, Loup celebrates and stamps it with a gold full stop.

YOUR READING TIME

A band on every card counts the minutes you've read today. Tap it for a month chart, one bar per day, against a daily goal you set — five minutes a day works out to about 30 hours a year. Loup counts the days in a row you meet that goal, on the card and on the chart, and a broken streak can be earned back the next day.

Turn on a daily reminder in Profile if you want one — off until you turn it on.

FREE, HONESTLY

Loup is free, with an occasional "Sponsored" card in the feed, never inside a book you're following. There's no account to create and nothing to subscribe to. The feed also works offline, from a local reserve of cards.

Questions, or a card that looks wrong? Use Report on any card, or write to supportloup@gmail.com.
